'''Md. Hanifuddin Miah''' (1 November 1929 – 11 March 2007) was a [[Bangladeshis|Bangladeshi]] [[physicist]] and [[mathematician]]. He is recognized as the first [[computer programmer]] of [[Bangladesh]] (then [[East Pakistan]]). In 1964, he was one of the few experts trained to operate the country's first [[computer]], an [[IBM 1620]], installed at the [[Atomic Energy Centre, Dhaka]], and served as its chief programmer.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rahman |first1=Sadikur |title=Bangladesh's first computer and the man behind its arrival here |url=https://www.tbsnews.net/feature/panorama/bangladeshs-first-computer-and-man-behind-its-arrival-here-94324 |publisher=[[The Business Standard]] |access-date=25 February 2026 |date=18 June 2020 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Abu Jar M Akkas |title=Bangla computing: follies all the way |url=https://www.newagebd.net/post/Victory%20Day%20Special%202021/157436/bangla-computing-follies-all-the-way |publisher=[[New Age (Bangladesh)]] |access-date=28 February 2026 |date=16 December 2021}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite news |title=মরণোত্তর সম্মাননা পেলেন দেশের প্রথম কম্পিউটার প্রোগ্রামার |trans-title=Posthumous award for the country's first computer programmer |url=https://www.prothomalo.com/technology/%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%A3%E0%A7%8B%E0%A6%A4%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%AE%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A8%E0%A6%A8%E0%A6%BE-%E0%A6%AA%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B2%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%A8-%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B6%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%AA%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%A5%E0%A6%AE-%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%AE%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AA%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%89%E0%A6%9F%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0 |newspaper=[[Prothom Alo]] |date=19 June 2015 |access-date=1 March 2026 |language=bn}}</ref>

==Early life==
Hanifuddin Mia was born on 1 November 1929 in Hulhulia village of Chowgram Union (No. 10), [[Singra Upazila]], in the [[Natore District]]. Among the two sons and one daughter of [[Teacher|schoolteacher]] Rajab Ali Talukdar and his mother Naziron Bibi, Hanifuddin Mia was the eldest. Although the family was not poor, he had to live as a ''jaigir'' (a form of lodging in exchange for work) in order to pursue higher education.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kumar |first=Tapash |date=13 April 2021 |title=যেসব কারণে যাওয়ার ইচ্ছে জাগবে নাটোরের হুলহুলিয়ায় [Reasons That Will Make You Want to Visit Hulhulia in Natore] |url=https://www.dhakapost.com/country/24088 |access-date=11 March 2026 |work=[[Dhaka Post]] |language=bn}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Jabbar |first=Mustafa |date=10 December 2017 |title=একুশ শতক ॥ বাংলার প্রথম প্রোগ্রামার [21st Century {{!}}{{!}} The First Programmer of Bengal] |url=https://www.dailyjanakantha.com/opinion/news/313076 |access-date=11 March 2026 |work=Daily Janakantha |language=bn}}</ref>

==Academic career==
He passed the [[Matriculation examination]] in 1946 under the [[University of Calcutta]].<ref name=":0" /> In 1948, he passed the ISc examination (equivalent to the present-day [[Higher Secondary Certificate|HSC]]) under the [[University of Dhaka]] with a First Division. After completing his undergraduate studies, he secured first place in the First Class in the [[Bachelor of Science|BSc examination]] in 1951. In 1952, he completed his [[Master's degree|Master’s degree (MSc)]] in [[Applied mathematics|Applied Mathematics]] from the [[University of Dhaka]]. In this examination, he again demonstrated exceptional merit by achieving first place in the First Class and was awarded a [[gold medal]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=18 November 2024 |title=৬০ বছর আগে বাংলাদেশের প্রথম কম্পিউটার এসেছিল যার হাত ধরে [The person through whom Bangladesh's first computer arrived 60 years ago] |url=https://www.dhakatoday.com/news/43154/%E0%A7%AC%E0%A7%A6-%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%9B%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%86%E0%A6%97%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%82%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B6%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%AA%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%A5%E0%A6%AE-%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%AE%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AA%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%89%E0%A6%9F%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%8F%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%9B%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B2-%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%B9%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A4-%E0%A6%A7%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%87 |access-date=11 March 2026 |work=Dhaka Today |language=bn}}</ref>

After completing his formal education, he went abroad for advanced training. In 1960, he received training in analog and digital [[computer programming]] from the [[Institute of Information Theory and Automation of the CAS|Institute of Information Theory and Automation]] in [[Prague]], then part of [[Czechoslovakia]], and from the [[Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences]]. In 1964, he obtained training at the Computer Center of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)]] in the United States in [[systems analysis]], [[Numerical analysis|numerical mathematics]], advanced [[computer programming]], and [[operations research]]. Later, in 1975, he also received advanced training in [[Operating system|operating systems]] and [[Systems programming|system programming]] at the [[IBM|IBM Research Center]] in [[London]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sharif |first=Mahbub |date=2 November 2019 |title=একজন কম্পিউটার বিপ্লবের জাতীয় বীর [A National Hero of Computer Revolution] |url=https://www.ittefaq.com.bd/102085/%E0%A6%8F%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%9C%E0%A6%A8-%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%AE%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AA%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%89%E0%A6%9F%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AA%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%AC%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%9C%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A4%E0%A7%80%E0%A7%9F-%E0%A6%AC%E0%A7%80%E0%A6%B0 |access-date=11 March 2026 |work=[[The Daily Ittefaq]] |language=bn}}</ref>

== Career ==
Md. Hanifuddin Mia is known as one of the pioneers of the early era of [[Computing|computer technology]] in [[Bangladesh]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=10 January 2022 |title=বাংলাদেশে প্রথম কম্পিউটার এসেছিল কখন? [When did the First Computer Come to Bangladesh?] |url=https://www.somoynews.tv/news/2022-01-10/%E0%A6%AA%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%A5%E0%A6%AE-%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%96%E0%A6%A8-%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%AE%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AA%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%89%E0%A6%9F%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%82%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B6%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%8F%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%9B%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B2%E0%A7%8B |access-date=11 March 2026 |work=Somoy TV |language=bn}}</ref> In 1964, the [[United States]] government presented [[Pakistan]] with an [[IBM 1620]] computer as a gift. Initially, it was decided that the computer would be installed at the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] in [[Lahore]], [[West Pakistan]], and plans were made to ship it to the [[Karachi]] seaport accordingly. However, no trained programmer was available in [[West Pakistan]] to operate the machine. In this situation, the authorities proposed that Hanifuddin Mia—who had received training abroad—move to [[Lahore]]. Out of deep attachment to his homeland, however, he refused to go there despite various incentives. Because of his firm stance, the [[Pakistan|Pakistani]] government was compelled to send the computer to [[Port of Chittagong|Chittagong seaport]] instead of [[Karachi]]. It was later installed at the office of the [[Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission|Dhaka Atomic Energy Commission]], and through Hanifuddin Mia’s efforts the formal journey of computers in [[Bangladesh]] began.<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 March 2023 |title=হানিফউদ্দিন মিয়া-বাংলাদেশের প্রথম কম্পিউটার প্রোগ্রামার [Hanifuddin Miah-The First Computer Programmer of Bangladesh] |url=https://natore.org/hanifuddin-miah/#:~:text=%E0%A6%AE%E0%A7%8B.%20%E0%A6%B9%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A8%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AB%20%E0%A6%89%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A6%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A8%20%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A5%A4%20%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%AE%20%E0%A6%AA%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%9A%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A4%20%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A4%E0%A7%81,%E0%A6%B9%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A8%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AB%E0%A6%89%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A6%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A8%20%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BC%E0%A6%BE%20%E0%A6%93%20%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B6%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B0%20%E0%A6%AA%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%A5%E0%A6%AE%20%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%AE%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AA%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%89%E0%A6%9F%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B0%20%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%B2%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AA%E0%A5%A4 |url-access=registration |website=নাটোরবাসী}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=17 June 2015 |title=দেশে প্রথম কম্পিউটার এসেছিল যাঁর হাত ধরে [The Person through whom the First Computer in the Country Arrived] |url=https://www.ntvbd.com/tech/11994/%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B6%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%AA%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%A5%E0%A6%AE-%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%AE%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AA%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%89%E0%A6%9F%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%8F%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%9B%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B2-%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%81%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%B9%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A4-%E0%A6%A7%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%87 |access-date=11 March 2026 |work=NTV Online |language=bn}}</ref>

Later, he served as the Director of the Computer Service Division of the [[Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission]]. He also worked internationally; from 1975 to 1980, he served as a [[systems analyst]] at the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]]. During his professional life, he taught mathematics and computer science at various institutions. As part of this work, he joined the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of Dhaka]] as a part-time lecturer in 1988. He was also one of the founding members of the [[Bangladesh Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Roy |first=Alkananda |date=29 December 2022 |title=কম্পিউটার বিপ্লবের জাতীয় বীর মো. হানিফ উদ্দিন মিয়া [Md. Hanifuddin Miah, National Hero of Computer Revolution] |url=https://www.ajkerpatrika.com/technology/ajpwsy4tbbxiv |access-date=11 March 2026 |work=Ajker Patrika |language=bn}}</ref>

A polyglot, Hanifuddin Mia was proficient not only in [[Bengali language|Bengali]] and [[English language|English]] but also in [[Urdu]], [[Arabic]], [[Hindi]], [[German language|German]], and [[Russian language|Russian]]. In April 1997, [[Bangladesh Television]] broadcast the country’s first program on computers, in which IT specialist [[Mustafa Jabbar|Mostafa Jabbar]] interviewed him. In that interview, he publicly described the historical background behind the arrival of the first computer in the country.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jabbar |first=Mustafa |date=27 June 2015 |title=তিনি পাকিস্তানে যেতে রাজি না হওয়ায় আমরা কম্পিউটারটি পাই [We Got the Computer Because He Refused to Move to Pakistan] |url=https://www.kalerkantho.com/print-edition/oboshore/2015/06/27/238142 |access-date=11 March 2026 |work=[[Kaler Kantho]] |language=bn}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
In his family life, Hanifuddin Mia was the husband of Farida Begum and the father of one son and two daughters. His son, Sharif Hasan Suja, is an [[engineer]] who worked at Siemens Bangladesh for 23 years and is currently employed at a private housing company. One of his daughters, Dora Shirin, is a [[Medical doctor|physician]], while the other daughter, Nita Shaheen, is a homemaker.<ref name=":0" />

== Death ==
Hanifuddin Mia passed away on 11 March 2007 at the age of 77.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rahitul |first=Islam |date=22 June 2015 |title=তাঁরই হাত ধরে [Holding His Hand] |url=https://www.prothomalo.com/technology/%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%81%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%87-%E0%A6%B9%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A4-%E0%A6%A7%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%87 |access-date=11 March 2026 |work=[[Prothom Alo]] |language=bn}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
The first computer used in [[Bangladesh]] was preserved in 2001 at the [[National Museum of Science and Technology (Bangladesh)|National Museum of Science and Technology]] in [[Agargaon|Agargaon, Dhaka]]. Earlier, in 2000, Hanifuddin Mia donated two [[IBM]] desktop computers to Hulhulia High School in his native village. As a result of this initiative, IT education began to expand in the village. Later, along with doctors, more than a hundred engineers emerged from that village, which is considered a result of his far-sighted initiative.<ref name=":0" />

== Honors & Recognition ==
On 17 June 2015, he was posthumously honoured at the Bangladesh ICT Expo, organized by the [[Information and Communication Technology Division|ICT Division]] and the [[Bangladesh Computer Society]], in recognition of his outstanding contribution as the first computer [[programmer]] in Bangladesh. The then [[Ministry of finance|Finance Minister]] [[Abul Maal Abdul Muhith]] presented the commemorative award to his family.<ref name=":1" />

On 31 October 2019, a commemorative [[postage stamp]] worth 10 taka was released in his memory at the auditorium of the [[Bangladesh Post Office]] in [[Dhaka]]. At the event, the Minister of Posts and Telecommunications [[Mustafa Jabbar]] described Hanifuddin Mia as a “national hero” and called for his biography to be included in school textbooks.<ref>{{Cite news |date=31 October 2019 |title=বরেণ্য কম্পিউটার প্রোগ্রামার হানিফ জাতীয় বীর [Renowned Computer Programmer Hanif is a National Hero] |url=https://www.bhorerkagoj.com/2019/10/31/%e0%a6%ac%e0%a6%b0%e0%a7%87%e0%a6%a3%e0%a7%8d%e0%a6%af-%e0%a6%95%e0%a6%ae%e0%a7%8d%e0%a6%aa%e0%a6%bf%e0%a6%89%e0%a6%9f%e0%a6%be%e0%a6%b0-%e0%a6%aa%e0%a7%8d%e0%a6%b0%e0%a7%8b%e0%a6%97%e0%a7%8d%e0%a6%b0 |access-date=11 March 2026 |work=Vorer Kagoj |language=bn}}</ref>
